definitions.explanation: Describes feelings of dislike or discomfort toward something.
Used when someone is unwilling to do something.

examples.japanese: {嫌|いや}な⟦{予感|よかん}→予感：11416_yokan⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧。
{嫌|いや}な{臭|にお}い⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧。
{嫌|いや}な⟦{思|おも}い{出|で}→思い出：00331_omoide⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{思|おも}い{出|だ}した→思い出す：01258_omoidasu⟧。
「⟦{行|い}きたくない→行く：00119_iku⟧」「{嫌|いや}だ」
⟦{野菜|やさい}→野菜：02265_yasai⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{食|た}べる→食べる：00396_taberu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{嫌|いや}だ。
{嫌|いや}なら⟦{無理|むり}しなくて→無理する：22426_murisuru⟧⟦いい→いい：00118_ii⟧⟦よ→よ：09475_yo⟧。
examples.english: If you don't want to, you don't have to force yourself.

notes:
{嫌|いや} is a na-adjective expressing strong dislike, discomfort, or unwillingness. It is one of the most common ways to express negative feelings in everyday Japanese.

USAGE:
- {嫌|いや}だ: direct refusal or expression of dislike ("No way" / "I don't want to")
- {嫌|いや}な + noun: modifies a noun to mean unpleasant or disagreeable
- ⟦{嫌|いや}になる→嫌になる：20664_iyaninaru⟧: to get sick of, to become fed up with

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {嫌|いや}な⟦{予感|よかん}→予感：11416_yokan⟧: a bad feeling
- {嫌|いや}な{気持|きも}ち: an unpleasant feeling
- {嫌|いや}な{臭|にお}い: an unpleasant smell
- {嫌|いや}な⟦{思|おも}い→思い：10248_omoi⟧: an unpleasant experience/memory

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{嫌|きら}い→嫌い：02871_kirai⟧: expresses dislike as a personal preference ("I don't like X"), while {嫌|いや} emphasizes the feeling of aversion or reluctance in the moment
- ⟦{不快|ふかい}→不快：11386_fukai⟧: more formal/literary word for unpleasant
